newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines hikes power rates in most grids.
newsitem.headline: Philippines hikes power rates in most grids.

text.p: The Philippines National Power Corp (Napocor) said on Monday it raised power rates by 14.19 centavos in the main northern island of Luzon.
Napocor increased power rates in most grids effective October 26 citing higher cost of power purchased from privately-owned power plants.
Customers of Napocor in Luzon will now pay 2.3171 pesos per kilowatt-hour (kwh) from the previous month's 2.1752 pesos.
In central Philippines, Napocor raised rates in the Cebu-Negros-Panay grid by 5.77 centavos per kwh, and the Bohol grid by 5.36 centavos.
Napocor lowered rates in the Leyte-Samar grid by 0.37 centavos and in the southern island of Mindanao by 0.66 centavos per kwh.

The state-run power firm adjusts power rates monthly based on an automatic formula that passes on increases or decreases in the prices of fuels used to run the plants as well as the movement of the peso versus major currencies.
